welcome.startSub: A short, thoughtful intro and a few personal touches
welcome.skipSub: I'll figure it out as I go

profile.title: Why we're asking
paragraphs: Your name and what you do help us fit the system to you — the language on screen, the default categories, how clients and groups are shown.
You can change any of it later in Settings.

data_import.title: How the import works
paragraphs: If you have a table (Excel / CSV) with clients, projects or transactions, you can upload it and we'll pull out what we can.
Whatever we find comes through filled in on the next steps, and you can approve or edit every row before anything is saved.
bullets: You can upload more than once
Entirely optional — you can start from scratch

projects.title: What is a project?
paragraphs: A project is the wider context — the kind of service, the kind of work, or a working group. For example "one-on-one coaching", "parenting workshops", "couples therapy".
Every client belongs to one project. Clients in the same project share the same goals, income calculations and groups.
bullets: Group (inside a project) = a cohort with a start and end date
Client = one person, who belongs to a project

clients.title: What is a client?
paragraphs: A client is one person you work with. Each one has a status (active / on a break / former), a project, and sometimes a package of sessions.
From the client's card you can log meetings, take a payment, and book the next session.

daily_questions.title: How the questions work
paragraphs: One question appears each day. A short answer on any given day lets the system build a wider picture over time.
Questions from our suggestions also feed the graphs and "Overview". Your own questions are more for reflection — we don't analyse those automatically.

goals.title: Goals tie everything together
paragraphs: A goal is a direction, not pressure. It takes a number (how many clients, how much income, how many enquiries), a time frame, and how much it matters to you.
Income goals feed the money graphs and "Overview". Other goals show up mainly in "Overview" and "Reports".

recurring.title: Why record fixed expenses once
paragraphs: Income and expenses that repeat (rent, insurance, a subscription, a monthly package) are created for you every month as a pending transaction.
All you do is confirm they really happened — no re-entering them each time.

preview.title: What are we looking at?
paragraphs: A preview of what your data builds up to over time: an income graph, the weighted "Overview" score, progress against the goals you set.
The more transactions, meetings and daily answers there are, the more the picture starts to say something real.

finish.title: On to the home screen
paragraphs: The home screen is built from widgets. You choose which ones appear, in what order, and in what colour.
You can set it all up again from "Settings → Widgets and display".

why.schema: A field that doesn't exist here — probably a column mapped to the wrong place.
why.duplicate: You already have an identical item.
why.check: One of the values isn't valid (for example an unfamiliar date or status).

why.noConnection: The connection dropped — you'll need to reconnect.

modal.noData: We didn't find any data in the file — make sure it isn't empty and that it's saved as CSV or Excel.
modal.truncated: Some sheets were cut to their first rows to keep things fast. You can import the rest in a separate file later.

modal.notReady: Choose what's in each sheet and map the name / amount columns.

sheet.matrixIntro: Mark each row as income or expense. "Skip" leaves a row out (a totals row, for example).

typeHelp.clients: A client list — name, phone, status, sessions and so on.
typeHelp.projects: A list of projects, programmes or tracks.
typeHelp.leads: Enquiries and interested people who haven't become clients yet.
typeHelp.transactions: One row per payment or expense, with a date and an amount.
typeHelp.sessions: A log of meetings that already happened — one row per meeting.
typeHelp.matrix: A table where the months are columns and each row is an income or expense line.
